Description:
Problem:
When Cursor imports a session into the CLI, it may prepend a <timestamp> tag to prompts before the <user_query> tag. The CLI was already stripping <user_query> tags from imported prompts, but the timestamp block was not being removed, leaving metadata in the stored prompt text.
Solution:
Added a regex pattern to StripIDEContextTags that removes Cursor's injected <timestamp> blocks while preserving the actual prompt content. The pattern matches timestamp tags with optional attributes and removes them from single-line contexts. Updated the Cursor agent documentation to note this behavior. Added test cases covering timestamp removal with various formats (with/without attributes) and edge cases (nested tags, timestamps in pasted XML).

8	// ideContextTagRegex matches IDE-injected context tags like <ide_opened_file>...</ide_opened_file>
9	// and <ide_selection>...</ide_selection>. These are injected by the VSCode extension.
10	var ideContextTagRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)<ide_[^>]*>.*?</ide_[^>]*>`)

13	// Each tag type needs its own regex since Go's regexp doesn't support backreferences.

15		regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)<local-command-caveat[^>]*>.*?</local-command-caveat>`),
16		regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)<system-reminder[^>]*>.*?</system-reminder>`),
17		regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)<command-name[^>]*>.*?</command-name>`),
18		regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)<command-message[^>]*>.*?</command-message>`),

20		regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)<local-command-stdout[^>]*>.*?</local-command-stdout>`),
21		regexp.MustCompile(`</?user_query>`),                              // Cursor wraps user text in <user_query> tags; strip tags but keep content
22		regexp.MustCompile(`<timestamp(\s[^>]*)?>[^<\n]*</timestamp\s*>`), // Cursor-injected send-time date; single-line body only
23	}
24	
25	// StripIDEContextTags removes IDE-injected context tags from prompt text.
26	// The VSCode extension injects tags like:
27	//   - <ide_opened_file>...</ide_opened_file> - currently open file
28	//   - <ide_selection>...</ide_selection> - selected code in editor
29	//
30	// Also removes system-injected tags like:
31	//   - <local-command-caveat>...</local-command-caveat>
32	//   - <system-reminder>...</system-reminder>
33	//   - <command-name>...</command-name>
34	//
35	// These shouldn't appear in commit messages or session descriptions.
36	func StripIDEContextTags(text string) string {
37		result := ideContextTagRegex.ReplaceAllString(text, "")
38		for _, re := range systemTagRegexes {
39			result = re.ReplaceAllString(result, "")

content.text:
Done. Both open findings on trail 1087 are addressed and resolved.

**What the findings said:** Both flagged the same defect in `cmd/entire/cli/textutil/ide_tags.go:22` — the `<timestamp>` regex matched anywhere in the prompt, so a user pasting XML or log text containing `<timestamp>2026-01-01</timestamp>` would have it silently deleted. Unlike the other stripped tags (`ide_*`, `local-command-*`), `timestamp` is ordinary XML vocabulary, so name alone can't distinguish Cursor's injection from user content.

**The fix (commit `979cbea67` on `fix/import-prompt-tags`):** Anchored the regex with `\A\s*`, so only a single-line `<timestamp>` block at the head of the message is stripped. That matches Cursor's actual injection shape — it prepends the send-time date before `<user_query>` (documented in `cursor/AGENT.md`). The trade is deliberate: a timestamp arriving anywhere else now leaks into a title at worst (cosmetic false negative), instead of ever corrupting user content.

Along the way:
- Updated the two test cases that had been pinning the old behavior — the pasted-XML case now asserts a leading timestamp is stripped while the embedded one survives, and the nested-`<timestamps>` case asserts full preservation.
- Noted the anchoring in the Cursor `AGENT.md` behavior list.
- Tests pass for `textutil`, `agentimport`, `agent/cursor`, and both `transcript` packages; fmt + lint clean.
- The remote branch had picked up a merge of `main` while I worked, so I rebased my single unpushed commit on top rather than force-pushing anything.
- Resolved both findings (the current one and the stale duplicate from the earlier code version) via the cell API with a `statusReason` pointing at the commit — the installed nightly's `entire trail finding resolve` still 400s, so I used the `entire api` workaround.
